transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-09-10 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~62m | Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Natarajan (Redwood SE), Alex Moreno (Novus Head of ML Ops), Maria Chen (CTO), Samir Patel (SRE)

[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you carving out time. Quick agenda: confirm success criteria, agree benchmarks and reporting format, and lock timeline.
[00:12] Alex Moreno: Yeah thanks, Jordan. We want to make sure the POC proves both performance and cost improvements vs our current setup, and that security/code path meets our audit needs.
[00:23] Priya Natarajan: Great, I have the draft success criteria up — I'll read through and we can iterate. Note, some typos in my slides earlier, "Redwood Dedic8d" is actually Redwood Dedicated, sorry for the voice to text fun.
[00:36] Maria Chen: Haha, no worries. On security, we need KMS integration and audit logging; we are SOC2 required and also need to show data residency in US-East for these records.
[00:47] Priya Natarajan: Understood. We'll plan for KMS/HSM key wrap and include audit logs. We'll also propose a private VPC peering flow for the on-prem-like traffic — I might say V P C a few times weirdly in the doc.
[01:00] Jordan Lee: Ok success criteria item 1: Latency — target P95 latency under 150ms for a 512-token generation for typical prompts, and P99 under 300ms when caching is warm. Does that align with your expectations?
[01:15] Samir Patel: 150ms P95 is aggressive but acceptable if it's measured end-to-end from our app to the Redwood endpoint. We need to define measurement points. Also please include cold-start behavior.
[01:30] Priya Natarajan: We'll instrument both client-to-edge and edge-to-gpu layers in the report; acceptance test will include cold-start (first-request) and warmed KV cache runs. Cold-start P95 we expect higher, we'll set a go/no-go threshold at 500ms.
[01:45] Alex Moreno: Good. Next — throughput. We need sustained throughput of 120 concurrent users with average 0.5 reqs/sec per user during peak, so roughly 60 RPS sustained with 95th percentile latency under the P95 target.
[02:00] Priya Natarajan: Noted. We'll run a load profile that ramps to 60 RPS sustained for 30 minutes and measure across multiple seeds.
[02:14] Jordan Lee: Success criteria item 3: Cost. You mentioned wanting to be cost-neutral vs current infra; can you remind us the current token cost?
[02:23] Alex Moreno: Roughly $10 per 1k tokens after our optimizations; our internal bar is to be at or below $8/1k for the same quality.
[02:34] Priya Natarajan: For the POC we'll report cost per effective 1k tokens in the canonical run, and propose batching / quantization settings to reach that. Acceptance threshold: average cost <= $8/1k tokens across benchmark runs.
[02:50] Maria Chen: On quality — we will use our internal prompt set of 200 prompts and expect >= 95% parity on the primary metrics (intent accuracy / response completeness). If automatic metrics are ambiguous we'll do a small human eval sample (20 items) and expect no more than 2 regressions.
[03:10] Priya Natarajan: We'll deliver the benchmark output as a CSV and a short dashboard snapshot with the following columns: prompt_id, latency_p50, latency_p95, latency_p99, tokens_in, tokens_out, cost_per_1k_tokens, quality_flag, notes. We'll also attach the raw logs and a summarized PDF.
[03:30] Jordan Lee: Sounds good. Let's be explicit about go/no-go: all must pass or we fail? How strict do you want it?
[03:40] Alex Moreno: Prefer a majority of criteria must be met. Proposal: hard fail if latency or security doesn't meet thresholds, soft fail if cost slightly over but with a proposed remediation plan. That gives us room.
[03:55] Priya Natarajan: Agreed. We'll label criteria as Critical (latency, security, data residency), Important (throughput, cost), Nice-to-have (autoscaling responsiveness). Go/no-go rules: any Critical fail is a no-go; Important fails require mitigation plan and re-test.
[04:12] Samir Patel: On reporting frequency — we want daily benchmark artifacts during the 2-week run and a final sign-off report with raw files, dashboards and runbooks.
[04:24] Priya Natarajan: We'll produce daily CSVs plus an evaluation dashboard link (read-only), and a final sign-off package with a recommended configuration for production.
[04:36] Jordan Lee: Timeline check — proposed: week 1 (2025-09-15) infra and endpoint setup + SSO and KMS config, week 2 (2025-09-22) baseline and tuned benchmark runs, week 3 (2025-09-29) final report and go/no-go decision. Is that realistic?
[04:55] Alex Moreno: That's fine. We may need a short buffer for legal review of the DPA but ops can run the tests.
[05:06] Maria Chen: Who owns the test harness? We prefer Redwood to run initial harness but provide terraform snippets to mirror setup in our staging.
[05:16] Priya Natarajan: Redwood will run the initial benchmark harness using your provided dataset; we'll provide the harness repo and Terraform snippets for VPC peering. We'll also give a one-day handover to your SREs.
[05:29] Jordan Lee: Good. Acceptance test details recap:
- Critical: Latency (P95 < 150ms for 512 token w/ warm cache), Security (SOC2 + KMS + audit logs), Data residency in us-east.
- Important: Sustained throughput 60 RPS with P95 latency target, Cost <= $8/1k tokens average.
- QA: >=95% parity on 200 prompt set or <=2 human-eval regressions on sample.
[06:00] Samir Patel: For benchmarking seeds, please include both standard prompts and adversarial edge cases. We also want to measure memory usage and inference GPU utilization.
[06:10] Priya Natarajan: We'll include GPU utilization and memory footprint in the raw logs. Kernel selection notes: we'll test both q4_0 and q8_0 quant profiles to see cost vs perf tradeoff, noting that some model ops may change with quantization.
[06:30] Alex Moreno: Any competitors or alternative we'll compare to? We ran a baseline against Anthropic last quarter, openai earlier. For this POC we just need Redwood vs our in-house stack.
[06:42] Jordan Lee: Ok noted.
[06:45] Maria Chen: A couple of smaller asks: 1) an explicit CSV column for request timestamp and request id so we can correlate in our tracing, 2) a simple scoring rubric for human eval.
[06:58] Priya Natarajan: We'll add request_id and timestamp columns. For human eval rubric: 0 = wrong, 1 = partially correct, 2 = correct, with brief justification. We'll include the rubric in the final package.
[07:12] Jordan Lee: Before we close, any blockers?
[07:15] Alex Moreno: Legal may ask for a DPA - we have one queued but it might take a week. Not a blocker for running benchmarks on non-prod data.
[07:25] Samir Patel: We'll share the sample S3 link and IAM read-only role by tomorrow.
[07:30] Jordan Lee: Great. Quick recap of next steps and owners (I'll follow up in email): Jordan - pricing + security pack; Priya - harness + terraform + CSV schema; Alex - sample dataset + concurrency profile; Samir - network details. We'll target first benchmark runs week of 2025-09-15 and decision by 2025-09-29.
[07:50] Maria Chen: Confirmed from Novus side. Alex and Samir will sign-off on the acceptance criteria after we get the written doc.
[07:58] Alex Moreno: Yep, we will sign off once the doc includes the exact CSV fields and go/no-go rules you stated.
[08:05] Jordan Lee: Excellent, thank you all. We'll circulate the finalized doc today and set up the infra kickoff.
[08:12] (end)

Notes: minor transcription issues: "Redwood Dedic8d" = Redwood Dedicated, "K-V cash" = KV cache, some speakers labeled generically in the raw export.

References shared during call: link: https://redwood.ai/poc-checklist (DEMO deck), ephemeral: /shared/novus/sample-prompts.csv, benchmark harness repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/bench-harness (private)

Final sign-off line in chat: Alex Moreno: "Novus signs off on success criteria as discussed, pending written doc and DPA clearance"
